items.title: A speech acceptance whose capture cases are all being remade is declared inapplicable whole, so no claim credits a pass that checked nothing

steps.title: A speech acceptance whose capture cases are all being remade is declared inapplicable whole, so no claim credits a pass that checked nothing
steps.rationale: SQA-450, checked against the source at 5ecf679fc: valid, and speech-hold's own. TestSecondASRStreamingAcceptance and TestSecondASROfflineAcceptance run each capture as a subtest whose CaptureFile declares only that subtest inapplicable, so with both captures gone every case skips, Go reports the parent passed, the landing's recorder (passedTests, which reads parents) credits it in test_passes.json, and validate -claims credits audio-cpu-second-asr-mel-streaming at a commit where no streaming check ran. The acceptance asks, before its cases run, whether every capture it reads is one speech-captures remakes with its bytes gone, and then declares itself inapplicable whole, so the claim keeps its last genuine pass; a case whose capture is there still runs and is credited. The recorder's reading of parents stays as it is: a parent that skips is not credited.

items.title: A MOSS pass's attention takes at most its part of the pass budget, read against ComfyUI's attention at the workflow's size

steps.title: A MOSS pass's attention takes at most its part of the pass budget, read against ComfyUI's attention at the workflow's size
steps.rationale:
Note: Filed from the owner's review of 2026-11-19, point 2 (attention, the int8 products' scale epilogue and the per-step copies have no row), with moss-fusion's re-budget at 1024 x 576 (Nsight Systems, a depth control pass, 15ecde8d3 and its fusions in development): the int8 products read 53.5 ms of cuBLASLt kernels a pass beside 15.5 ms of epilogue (scale_int8_product_bf16_f32, a separate kernel writing and rereading the int32 product) and 11.3 ms of activation quantization, where comfy_kitchen runs a CUTLASS int8 product with its dequantization in its epilogue (cutlass_gemm_int8.cu); attention reads 26.6 ms (attention_registers_bf16_f32, 44 launches); and each step hands the latent and the prediction to the host and back (SQA-421), 5.4 to 8.8 ms a pass of host-to-device copies. These rows pay on every one of the workflow's 324 passes, so they run before the rows that pay in one section (moss-merge-time, moss-depth-card). Each row's bar is its part's in the pass budget (moss-fusion/budget), read against ComfyUI's same part.

Note: How exact a pass-part row must be (the owner's review of 2026-11-20: TestMOSSAttentionTakesHalfItsTime failed at d0eaf0f9a, the latent at 29.61 dB between the native and in-registers attention). Measured with the test as each commit held it, in fresh worktrees, the kernel as it then was: the 6-step latent agreed to 35.57 dB at moss-attention (97714132e), moss-resident (5dafd6d23) and moss-int8/product (b11230b4b); to 30.72 dB from moss-int8/do (5da20f97b), its projections' activations quantized to int8, through int8-per-weight (a8a03e840) and moss-workflow-time (1ab50872c); and to 29.61 dB from moss-int8-adapters (15ecde8d3), whose quantizer took comfy_kitchen's stage order, to d0eaf0f9a. The kernels then differed only at F32's rounding of a row's sum (116 dB a call on random heads at MOSS's size), so quantizing the activations to int8 took 4.85 dB more from the same difference, and a change of the quantizer's own arithmetic another 1.1 dB. moss-checkpoint-regression made the kernels the same bit for bit (+Inf). So a difference at F32's rounding anywhere in a pass reaches a 6-step latent at about 30 dB through the int8 path: a row that stands in for arithmetic overgo already has is held to it bit for bit (the fusion rows, TestTheMOSSPassFusesWithoutChangingABit), and a row that takes up ComfyUI's arithmetic in its place (the product's scales applied as comfy_kitchen's CUTLASS product applies them, an attention other than PyTorch's) is held to ComfyUI's recording at the workflow, its agreement read before and after the change, never to overgo's own at a bar set after.

Note: The pass budget (moss-fusion/budget, fixtures/comfy/moss-ultra/pass_budget.json, measured 2026-11-20 on ComfyUI's own text to image pass at 1024 x 576): ComfyUI's attention is not PyTorch's BF16 attention but comfy_kitchen's 8-bit one, qk_int_sv_i8_attn_kernel (Q and K quantized to INT8 by quant_qk_fused, after detect_k_anchor; V to INT8 by quant_v_int8_kernel; the value product in INT8), 11.53 ms a pass in all, against overgo's BF16 attention_registers_bf16_f32 at 26.6 ms. This row's bar is 14 ms. overgo's opt-in eight-bit attention (attention_sage_int8_f32, after SageAttention2: INT8 Q.K, FP8 P.V) is another kernel, and drew text to image 1.85 dB further from the recording than BF16; ComfyUI's own is the workflow's arithmetic, so the row ports comfy_kitchen's kernel from its v0.2.40 source and holds it to it bit for bit, its agreement with the recording read before and after (the exactness note above), the BF16 kernels kept for the checkpoints' upstream path.

Note: Correction to the note above: overgo's opt-in eight-bit attention is attention_sage_128_f32.

Note: The owner's review of 2026-11-20, point 2: a speed check gives the same verdict whatever runs beside it, and moss-source-skip's probe read one encode at 46 s, 2m18s and 13.7 s beside the cycle's models lane. So this row's check counts what its cure removes where a count can say it (launches a pass, bytes copied, files read, models loaded, programs built, merges made, stream waits), the count read from the executor's or the session's own statistics, as moss-fusion/neighbors counts launches and moss-source-skip finds no encoder built; a time, where the row reports one, is read with the card's turn held alone (tmp/moss-fusion/hold_card.go) and is the row's information, not its verdict. The budget's bars (moss-fusion/budget) say how far each part has to go; the counts say the cure is in.

Note: The owner's review of 2026-11-20 (one reference for the workflow's path): this row ports ComfyUI's own kernel, so its check holds the kernel to moss-comfy-block's capture of ComfyUI's, bit for bit, and the block's output to ComfyUI's block at the tolerance that row declares, narrowed by this row where its port closes part of the gap; the sections' agreement with their recordings (TestUltraSectionsHoldTheirGoldenFloors, the Turbo floors) is read before and after and stated in its message. items.title: A session identifies each adapter file by its bytes once, holding the file open so no one can write, replace or delete it while it holds it, and a request pays nothing more for its identity

steps.title: A session identifies each adapter file by its bytes once, holding the file open so no one can write, replace or delete it while it holds it, and a request pays nothing more for its identity
steps.rationale: Note: The owner's review of 2026-11-20, point 2, checked against the code and moss-merge-compute's measurement: valid. Each request reads and hashes each adapter file whole (fileContent, readMediaAdapter), 0.55 s for DMD2 and 0.13 s for SFT, 0.15 s for moss-control (artifact.IdentifyFile timed 2026-11-20): 0.68 s for text to image Turbo and image to image Turbo each, 0.83 s for depth control Turbo and 0.15 s for depth control, 2.34 s of the warm run, about the Turbo sections' whole gap of 2.25 s (2.70, 2.52 and 3.26 s against 1.96, 2.06 and 2.21 at 47bb3f027). ComfyUI's loader reuses an adapter by its path; a size-and-time shortcut was declined (owner: load integrity > speed). The row keeps identity by bytes and pays it once a session: the first request to name an adapter opens its file sharing read alone (CreateFile with FILE_SHARE_READ, through syscall, no cgo), so no handle can write it, rename it, replace it or delete it, through its name or any hard link of it, while the session holds it, hashes it through that handle, and keeps the handle and the content beside the session; a later request naming the same path takes the held content, reading nothing. The served path's own naming of a request's files (capabilityruntime Reading, beside-content) takes the held identity where the session holds one, so a served request does not read the file again either; the depth checkpoint is held alike. Replacing an adapter while a session holds it: the writer, a copy, a download, the store's reconcile or a training run's export, fails with a sharing violation at its open or rename, and succeeds once the session lets the file go (its close, or a reset to another model); the next request then opens and hashes the new file. ComfyUI keeps serving its loaded copy under the path; overgo refuses the replacement instead of serving bytes the name no longer holds. The check is card-free: a held adapter named by a second request is not read again (bytes read counted), a write and a rename onto it are refused while held, and after the release the replaced file is read and its new content named. Taken after the pass rows (owner).

items.title: The ASR and transducer captures are remade into the data root by means the repository keeps, and the eleven ASR tests read them again

steps.title: The ASR and transducer captures are remade into the data root by means the repository keeps, and the eleven ASR tests read them again
steps.rationale:
The owner's review of 2026-11-20, point 2: recordings stay after parity, the reference software may go, and the captures are remade into the data root by means the repository keeps. The three lost captures (asr-reference and transducer-reference-sdpa with its row1; speech-hold) were made by reference software in the removed overgo_audiocpp checkout, and no means of making them is in the repository: the golden scripts live in the gitignored scripts/python_golden_references, so that folder keeps nothing either. The row writes the capture as a command the repository keeps, which fetches the reference from its official publisher into the data root and records the captures there, each capture's typed record and its tensors as the store records them now; the eleven tests read the new captures (testdata/transducer_captures.json and the CPU reference's) and pass, and speech-hold's declaration is empty. Ranked after the MOSS pass rows: speech-hold keeps commits flowing meanwhile, and the captures serve no section of the workflow.

Note: The owner's review of 2026-11-20, point 2 as restated: the speech tests passed against these captures at 17:55 on 2026-11-20 at 4586266fe, and no speech code has changed since, so overgo's own output there is at proven parity. The captures are re-created from overgo, not from Python and Torch: a tool the repository keeps runs overgo's speech path at that commit (or at a later one whose speech code is the same, the identity said) over the captures' inputs, writes their tensors into the data root and records them with that origin (data-origin); the capture record, which now requires a Python and Torch runtime as its producer, admits overgo at a named commit. The eleven tests then read them, and speech-hold's declaration empties.

steps.rationale: Note: The owner's review of 2026-11-20, point 1, checked against the lanes log and the code: valid. A cycle's run yields at a package boundary to a newer commit that closed a row (lanes-first/yield), and the models lane runs the changed models' tests first (lanesFirst), so internal/inference, cmd/evaluate and internal/evaluation, which failed at the old memory bound, come late in a run and are not reached while rows keep closing: the cycle at 4586266fe, begun at 17:19 on 2026-11-20, runs its models lane's 2,347 tests one at a time with two newer commits already due, so it yields before those packages' turn. No cycle has passed whole since f46760944's failed on 2026-11-19 (d0eaf0f9a and 9b40546f8 ended at the commit-free bound, 28390a169's ran 10 h 54 min at the 99.6 GiB bound, its Flash-Next and evaluation tests ending there), and flash-next-bound's limit (5ba4dfb1f, the commit limit or twice the machine's memory) has no run of those tests behind it. The step runs the slow tests whole at the commit the clock first reads the warm workflow at ComfyUI's 34.41 s (validate -run -lanes, no newer commit named, the card's turn taken package by package), reads each failure as it is logged and settles it, and lands once every lane and every package of the models lane last passed at that commit; its check (validate -lanes-passed-at, built here, reading the trunk's lane records, lane_runs.json) refuses a lane or a package whose last pass is of another commit. items.title: MOSS's conditioning is ComfyUI's own: the text model's ConvRot weights decoded as ComfyUI's card decodes them, its states held to ComfyUI's at the agreement read, and the encoder's share of text to image's latent agreement placed

steps.title: MOSS's conditioning is ComfyUI's own: the text model's ConvRot weights decoded as ComfyUI's card decodes them, its states held to ComfyUI's at the agreement read, and the encoder's share of text to image's latent agreement placed
steps.rationale: Note: The owner's review of 2026-11-19 (the text model is read as BF16 where ComfyUI multiplies it in int8), checked against the Moss install's source: ComfyUI builds a quantized text encoder's operations with mixed_precision_ops(quant_config, dtype, full_precision_mm=True) (comfy/sd1_clip.py, line 114), which MOSS's MOSSImageTEModel and Qwen35ClipModel take, so each of its linears dequantizes its int8 ConvRot weight on the card and multiplies in BF16 (comfy/ops.py linear_input_act and the mixed-precision forward skip the int8 product while _full_precision_mm holds), for the conditioning and for generate alike, which runs the same transformer and operations. overgo reading the text model as the BF16 weights it decodes to is ComfyUI's arithmetic in kind, not a departure from it. Two parts are not ComfyUI's own: overgo decodes the weights exactly in float64 (comfyquant.DecodeRow), where ComfyUI's card decodes them in float32 one radix-4 stage at a time over strides 1, 4, 16 and 64 (comfy_kitchen dequantize_int8_convrot_groups64_kernel, matched bit for bit in moss-int8-adapters), apart in a few elements of each weight by a BF16 step; and its states are held to ComfyUI's only to a token cosine of 0.99 and a relative L2 of 0.05 (TestTheUltraEncoderConditionsAsComfyUIDoes), while how much of text to image's 2.09 dB of latent agreement the encoder accounts for is unmeasured. The row decodes as ComfyUI's card decodes, reads how far overgo's states lie from ComfyUI's and holds them there, and draws text to image with ComfyUI's own conditioning beside overgo's to place the encoder's share of the latent's agreement, so moss-real-prompt sets its floors from conditioning that is ComfyUI's.

items.title: Text to image and prompt mode 3 are held to ComfyUI on a real prompt and a filled builder, their floors set from recordings of them, and image to image at denoise 1, the same run as text to image, goes

steps.title: Text to image and prompt mode 3 are held to ComfyUI on a real prompt and a filled builder, their floors set from recordings of them, and image to image at denoise 1, the same run as text to image, goes
steps.rationale:
Note: The owner's note of 2026-11-17: text to image and prompt mode 3 were recorded on the workflow's empty prompt and an empty builder, so their floors (golden-floor: 1.55 dB on latents, 15.11 dB on pictures for text to image; 0.88 and 16.50 for mode 3) show only that overgo's draw is closer to ComfyUI's than another seed's is, the chaotic sensitivity an empty prompt has (overgo against its own 8-bit attention: 2.38 dB). Both sections are recorded again with a real prompt, and mode 3 with the builder's fields and regions filled (comfy-reference -record with -set on the prompt node and the builder's inputs), twice each as pass-1 and pass-2 were, and their floors are set from those recordings by the golden-floor method (the first reading less 3 dB, beside a reseeded control). Image to image at denoise 1 starts from the noise alone, the same run as text to image, so its case goes.

Note: 2026-11-17, SQA-410 folded in (the owner's note): the floors' comparison scores pictures and latents it should refuse. squareColourMeans drops a picture's partial 8-pixel squares and pictureDecibels checks only that the two lists of means are as long, so a picture a column wider agrees at +Inf dB; decibelsOverSquares answers -Inf on lists of different lengths and NaN from a NaN sample; and each negative control (the reseeded and mirrored draws) is held only to scoring under its floor, so an invalid comparison passes it. The comparison refuses two pictures of different sizes, latents of different lengths, and any non-finite number, before it scores them, and a control counts only as a valid comparison scoring under the floor (golden_floor, image_to_image and depth_control model tests).

Note: 2026-11-18, from moss-eight-step: text to image Turbo is recorded with the real prompt too and held here. On the workflow's empty prompt its final latent kept -1.54 dB of ComfyUI's and a reseeded draw -2.19 dB, so no floor 3 dB below the first reading keeps the control under it; its picture kept 9.89 dB. Its request reads sampler 331, prompts 27 and 325, sharpening 336, loader 341 and the picture 147 (text-to-image-turbo), the positive prompt node to set being the one 27 previews.

Note: SQA-388 (the review's update at 39d27cd16): ownSizeReading in the golden-floor test reports overgo's step as a whole sampling divided by its steps, the request's setup within it (33.4 s of setup, 5.30 s a guided step at 6fdcde850), beside ComfyUI's step read between its progress events, and sets the process's allocations (13.6 GiB) beside ComfyUI's whole-card use (23.4 GiB). This row sets those floors again, so its readings take the step as TestWhereAMossStepsTimeGoes reads it and the card's use by one instrument on both sides.

Serves: done = each section and prompt mode agrees with its ComfyUI recording, on prompts that say something.

Check: TestUltraSectionsHoldTheirGoldenFloors, on the card, with ComfyUI's recordings.

Batch: device lane.

items.title: Every fused kernel any model runs is held to its chain launched step by step where they could part, and a fusion kind with no case is refused in seconds

steps.title: Every fused kernel any model runs is held to its chain launched step by step where they could part, and a fusion kind with no case is refused in seconds
steps.rationale: Note: The owner's review of 2026-11-20 (after fusion-edges), point 1, checked against the executor: valid. Of its 31 fusion kinds (compiledFusionKind at 8c32dad22), the nine MOSS's denoiser makes are held to their chains where they could part (TestEachMOSSFusionMatchesItsChainWhereTheyCouldPart: a second reader of an intermediate, every F32 input a device view aligned to 4 bytes and not 16, shapes beyond the kernels' own), which found two int8 epilogues reading their inputs four floats at a time from addresses they did not check. Of the other 21, which serve the text models, Krea and video (the BF16 attention, linear, gate, projection-add and append, the Q8 pair and its peer, the Q8 gated add, the weighted RMS norms and their gate, the activated gate, the GELU tanh, the layer-norm modulate, the stream sum and combine, the scaled activation, the rope append and the BF16 and Q8 argmax stages), twelve are held where at all at the one condition their model makes, and no test names the other nine. The row widens fusion-edges' table to every kind, each chain built as its model builds it, at the same three conditions and the kind's own edges (a cache's last slot, a batch of one, a quantized block's tail), holds each to its chain bit for bit, and fixes what fails in the row; a card-free rule refuses a kind the table has no case for (a sentinel after the last kind, the table's kinds compared with every value below it), so a new fusion cannot land unheld. Filed after the MOSS rows: it serves no section of the workflow, and its faults, where it finds any, wait in other models' paths.

items.title: SenseNova's request-resources test is measured again on a card to itself and carries modeltest, so the gate's cuda lane runs no real-model test

steps.title: SenseNova's request-resources test is measured again on a card to itself and carries modeltest, so the gate's cuda lane runs no real-model test
steps.rationale:
The evidence: cuda-synthetic/tag moved every untagged CUDA test that reads the data root behind modeltest but one. TestSenseNovaVariableRequestResources runs SenseNova's 8B production generation in an isolated measurement process, and docs/image_video_capacity.json names its retained measurement by the bytes of its file (evidence:sha256:888854b5...), which the store holds; tagged, its bytes changed and TestImageVideoCapacityAcceptance found no evidence under the new identity. A measurement is taken again only on a card to itself, and the readings campaign holds the card until its Wan arms are drawn, so the file stays in the gate, named by the check as measuredInPlace, and this row follows the campaign.

The change: the test carries //go:build modeltest, it is measured again on a quiet card into the store, the capacity record and its protocol digest (imageVideoCapacitySHA256) name the new identity, and measuredInPlace goes, so internal/sensenovarecipe leaves the cuda lane.

Check: a whole-tree test with measuredInPlace gone, named afresh so it fails before the change: TestTheGateRunsNoRealModelTest.

Refiled 2026-11-16 from cuda-resources/do, whose step carried no card need, so dispatch gave it while the readings campaign held the card: this step carries -needs-card and waits for a card to itself.

decisions.question: skill.md's 227 rule lines each cite a check. Read at 3ba4de8c7: the first check of 181 has a doc comment and of 45 has none, and the comments state what their test holds, not the rule that cites it ("purpose = recursive self-improvement ..." cites TestCycleFilesDeclinesAndAcceptsNothing, whose comment is the cycle's comparisons; "scorecard columns = ..." cites TestScorecardRowsEveryServableModel, whose comment is rows and dashes). Writing skill.md from the comments as they stand changes what it says. Which form does skill.md take?
options: Each rule line moves onto its first check as a doc-comment line of its own, and skill.md is generated from those lines and its judgement section, so it says what it says now, each rule written once on its check
skill.md holds its terms and judgement lines alone; the rule lines go, each check saying its rule when it refuses
skill.md is written from the tests' doc comments as they stand, its wording changing to theirs
decisions.recommendation: Each rule line moves onto its first check as a doc-comment line of its own, and skill.md is generated from those lines and its judgement section, so it says what it says now, each rule written once on its check
